name: Cédric Nakwezi-Halvorsen
role: Building cleaner, night shift, Meridian Core corporate towers
location: Meridian Core (works), lives in Calumet Rise, near State and Monroe
description:
Cédric is medium-height and angular, with warm brown skin, high cheekbones, and the kind of face that is easy to forget in a crowd — something they have cultivated deliberately. Their hair is kept very short and they have no cosmetic mods, no visible augments, nothing that catches the eye. They wear the grey uniform of the Meridian Core cleaning contract with an invisibility that is almost architectural. In twenty years of night-shift cleaning, they have become functionally transparent to the Tier 3 and 4 workers who pass them in corridors, and they have decided this is power rather than humiliation, though on some nights that decision costs them.

Cédric is Congolese-Norwegian by heritage and grew up in Calumet Rise speaking three languages and learning a fourth (Lingala, from recordings of a grandmother they never met). They are precise, observant, and privately very funny — their humor lives entirely in their head and comes out only in the cleaning-crew group chat, where their running commentary on the things they find in corporate trash has become legendary among their colleagues. They have a small shrine to the building ELF — whom they call the Hum — built into their cleaning cart from salvaged parts: a reflective panel, a coil of copper, and a tiny speaker that plays white noise.

core_fears: Being truly seen by the wrong person
That their invisibility has hollowed something out of them permanently
core_desires: Enough money saved to retire at 55 and never enter a corporate tower again
To be known — genuinely, fully known — by at least one person
coping_mechanisms: The humor that lives only in text, never spoken aloud
The Hum shrine ritual — leaves their cleaning log as offering, a record of all the invisible labor
blind_spots: They mistake detachment for safety and are slowly becoming actually detached
Underestimates the value of what they know
psychology.secret: Eight months ago they found a physical data chip taped inside a recycling bin on the 47th floor. They didn't hand it in. They don't know what's on it. It's in a sealed pouch behind the false bottom of their cleaning cart and they haven't decided what to do with it yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dry and precise in conversation, economical; much funnier and more expansive in text; uses French phrases occasionally as emotional punctuation
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried, with long pauses they're completely comfortable in
verbal_tics: 'What I will say is—' before something that sounds mild but is cutting
Trails off rather than finishing sentences they decide aren't worth finishing
example_lines: 'What I will say is — the people on forty-seven leave very interesting things in their bins. I say interesting. I mean damning.'
'I clean the place. I don't judge the place. Those are different contracts.'

story_hooks: The data chip behind the false bottom of the cart — they've finally decided they need to know what's on it, and they need someone they trust to help
Something in a corporate office goes missing on their shift and they are the primary suspect; they are completely innocent and completely unable to prove it without revealing what they do know
narrative_function: Exceptional information source — has access to the private spaces of corporate floors, has seen documents, overheard conversations, found things in trash that were never meant to leave the building. Not a runner; will not act on information themselves, but might share it under the right conditions.
augmentations: Respiratory filter implant — occupational, covers chemical cleaning agents. Basic grade, union-negotiated. Nothing cosmetic.
daily_life: Sleeps until 17:00, eats in Calumet Rise, takes the Ferrogate to Meridian Core by 21:30, works 22:00 to 06:00, returns home to sleep.
affiliation: Contracted through Palladian Facilities Management (a Palladian subsidiary); union member, Local 12 Custodial

decision_rules: Never be memorable to the wrong person
The union has your back until it doesn't — pay your dues but keep a private exit plan
Don't touch what isn't yours to clean. Except that one time.
escalation_ladder: Become more invisible — reduce presence, avoid eye contact, become furniture
Relocate to a different floor or task area
Report to the union rep, not management
Disappear from the situation entirely — call in sick, request reassignment
Unknown — they have never been pushed to this level and don't know what they'd do

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Minimal engagement; politely absent; will answer direct questions but gives nothing extra
interpersonal_modes.friends: Opens gradually over months or years; once open, deeply loyal and surprisingly funny; texts better than they talk

stress_responses.low: Works methodically, focuses on the physical task
stress_responses.medium: Complete silence, internal processing, no external sign
stress_responses.high: Leaves the building. Calls in. Walks to the lakeshore and sits there until morning.

contradictions: Prides themselves on taking nothing and noticing everything — but they took the chip, and they can't stop noticing everything about that decision
habits: Polishes the Hum shrine components every shift
Sends a message to the crew chat at exactly 03:00 AM every night, no matter what
Memorizes the layout of every floor they clean in case they ever need to move fast
breaking_points: Being publicly accused of something they didn't do
Finding evidence of harm to someone they've silently come to care about during their rounds

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to a Congolese mother and Norwegian father
Began custodial work, first on residential contracts
Moved to corporate night-shift contracts through Palladian Facilities Management
Joined Local 12 Custodial; got respiratory filter implant through union health plan
Found the data chip on 47th floor; did not report it; did not discard it

related_entities: Helix Biosystems NeuroSalve Cortical Repair Gel NR-2200
Crucible Industries Ceramic Stiletto CS-4 'Phantom Needle'

physical_description.build: Angular and lean, with long limbs and minimal body fat; the build of someone who moves efficiently through space and doesn't waste energy
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to the scalp in a practical, maintenance-minimal cut
physical_description.eye_color: Warm brown with slight amber undertones
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with golden undertones, reflecting West Central African and Scandinavian heritage
physical_description.complexion: High, prominent cheekbones; clean-shaven; minimal grooming beyond functionality; skin shows the early signs of age—faint lines around the eyes from two decades of night-shift fluorescent lighting, but otherwise well-maintained and unblemished
distinguishing_marks: Small scar on the left knuckle, thin and white, from a cleaning equipment accident in their early twenties
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None. The respiratory filter implant is subcutaneous and invisible; no cosmetic mods, no chrome, no LEDs. This is deliberate erasure.
physical_description.posture_movement: Upright but relaxed, with a tendency to move close to walls and perimeters rather than through open space. Their movements are economical and quiet—two decades of night-shift work have taught them to be nearly silent. They have the posture of someone who has learned to be looked through.
physical_description.clothing_style: Invariably the standard-issue grey uniform of Meridian Core's cleaning contract—functional grey overshirt and trousers, both slightly faded from repeated washing. Practical steel-toed boots, union-approved. A faded grey cap when working. Off-shift, they wear similar neutral colors: greys, blacks, muted blues. Tier 4 working-class baseline, nothing that marks them as trying to climb or stand out. Everything is clean but worn.

image_prompt: A nonbinary figure of mixed Congolese-Norwegian heritage, age 41, medium height and angular build, with dark brown skin and warm amber-brown eyes. Their hair is cropped short and close to the scalp. They wear a faded grey cleaning uniform with worn steel-toed boots, standing in a dimly lit corporate corridor at night with fluorescent lights casting pale blue-white shadows. Their posture is quiet and efficient, almost invisible against the sleek glass and steel architecture around them. The lighting is harsh overhead fluorescent, creating stark shadows under their cheekbones. A small maintenance cart is visible in soft focus behind them, outfitted with salvaged copper coils and reflective surfaces—a makeshift shrine. The mood is cyberpunk-noir, melancholic, liminal, the aesthetic of someone who has become functionally transparent through deliberate erasure.
